ipv6.description: Whether the load balancer answers on IPv6, where IPv6 is available. Left out, it does when the subnet has an active ::/0 route to its Network Gateway, or when there's no ipv4Address.
Turns IPv6 on or off. A load balancer with no IPv4 address keeps IPv6. Turning it off drains IPv6 connections for each listener's idle timeout first.

List a project's load balancers, newest first

post.description: Asynchronous: answers 202 with the operation that creates it, which takes minutes. With ipv6: true, or with no ipv4Address, the operation fails with 409 ipv6_unavailable if IPv6 can't be given to the load balancer; one with an ipv4Address that left ipv6 out is made with IPv4 only instead. It fails with 409 subnet_has_no_gateway_route without each family's route to the subnet's Network Gateway.

delete.description: Asynchronous. Removes its listeners and leaves its target groups unused. 409 load_balancer_referenced while a firewall rule names it.

patch.description: 409 load_balancer_provisioning while it isn't active yet, for a change of ipv6. lastChange tracks IPv6 being turned on or off.
